label: S0060
statement: statement: LEMMA (uniform collisions under one-sided absorption). Let A_n be a deterministic binary streaming machine with initial state q_n and transition maps delta_{n,0}, delta_{n,1}. Let R_n be the states reachable from q_n. Assume for every q in R_n, delta_{n,0}(delta_{n,0}(q))=delta_{n,0}(q) and delta_{n,1}(delta_{n,0}(q))=delta_{n,0}(q). Then for every n>=1, the two distinct equal-length words u_n=0^(2n) and v_n=0^n1^n have the same terminal state. Proof: Put x=delta_{n,0}(q_n), which is reachable. By the first identity, processing 0^(2n) reaches x: after its first zero the state is x, and each further zero fixes x. Processing 0^n1^n also reaches x: its first n zeros reach x, and the second identity says one following 1 fixes x; by induction all remaining 1s fix x because x remains reachable and delta_{n,1}(x)=x. Thus both words end at x. They are distinct since their final n symbols are respectively all 0 and all 1; their common length is 2n. Their indexed bits are constants determined by the position range, so both families are polylogtime-uniform AC0. This proves a collision construction for the stated one-sided absorption subclass only; it does not establish collisions for arbitrary admissible streamers or address the P=NP compressor.

statement: statement: LEMMA (uniform collision from equal transition powers). Let (A_n) be a family of deterministic binary streaming machines with initial state q_n and transition maps δ_{n,0}, δ_{n,1}. Suppose there is a function r(n)≥1 such that δ_{n,0}^{r(n)}(q_n)=δ_{n,1}^{r(n)}(q_n) for every n. Then the distinct equal-length words u_n=0^{r(n)} and v_n=1^{r(n)} reach the same terminal state. If the indexed bits of u_n and v_n are output by a polylogtime-uniform AC⁰ family, they form a polylogtime-uniform collision family. Proof: Iterating δ_{n,0} exactly r(n) times from q_n gives the terminal state of u_n; iterating δ_{n,1} exactly r(n) times gives that of v_n. These are equal by hypothesis. Since r(n)≥1, their first bits differ, so the words are distinct, and both have length r(n). The uniformity conclusion follows from the stated output-bit hypothesis. This generalizes the equal-square condition of S0061 to equal powers at the initial state, but does not establish that such powers exist for arbitrary admissible streamers or close the general W-D obligation.

statement: S-PP-POL-1: pp-definitions preserve polymorphisms (Boolean, finite arity, no constants) - see lemma text

structure.lemma: Scope: Boolean relations of finite arity; pp-definitions as an existential quantification over a conjunction of atoms and equalities; no constants. If S(x_1..x_m) = EXISTS y . phi(x,y) with phi a conjunction of atoms R(...) and equalities, and f is a polymorphism of R (f preserves R coordinatewise), then f preserves S. Proof: let s^1..s^k be tuples in S with witnesses y^1..y^k such that phi(s^j, y^j) holds. Each atom R(z_1..z_r) of phi holds for the k argument tuples (one per j), so applying f coordinatewise to these k R-tuples gives an R-tuple. Assign each variable v the vector of its values across j and set v -> f(vector). Every atom of phi then holds for the image assignment, equalities hold because f acts on identical value columns, so f(s^1..s^k) lies in S with witness f(y^1..y^k). Status: standard fact, recorded as a verified lemma; it is not progress on P vs NP or on the port/transfer target of Q-50565a6d2f.

statement: Assuming MMW19 Theorem 1.2, for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has a one-pass algorithm using poly(s) space and update time, with Sigma_3 SAT^A queries of O~(s)-bit length. Therefore no lower bound can exclude every algorithm in an augmented streaming model permitting these transitions. By PH nesting, the same holds for Sigma_k SAT^A-oracle models for each fixed k >= 3.
proof: MMW19 Theorem 1.2 supplies, for every such A and s, a correct one-pass algorithm with O~(s) space, O~(s^2) update time, and Sigma_3 SAT^A queries of length O~(s). These bounds are polynomial in s, so the algorithm belongs to the augmented model. For fixed k >= 3, Sigma_3^A predicates are contained in Sigma_k^A by padding the quantifier prefix with dummy blocks. Thus an alleged lower bound excluding every algorithm in the augmented model contradicts this algorithm. This argument makes no claim for k < 3 or for stricter resource or query-length bounds.

statement:
statement: Let k≥0 be fixed. Suppose R(c,x) is a uniformly specified predicate in Σ_k^P, with c and x given as inputs and one polynomial bound applying to all inputs. Define A* = {⟨c,x⟩ : R(c,x)} and A_c = {x : R(c,x)}. Then A*∈Σ_k^P and A_c={x:⟨c,x⟩∈A*} for every c.
proof: By definition, membership in A* is decided by the same Σ_k^P predicate R on input ⟨c,x⟩, so A*∈Σ_k^P under the stated uniform polynomial bound. For each fixed c, the section of A* obtained by fixing the first coordinate to c is exactly {x:R(c,x)}=A_c. The encoding map x↦⟨c,x⟩ is polynomial-time for each fixed c. Hence the family is represented by one oracle, with each member recovered by tagged queries. This statement concerns oracle membership and does not assert that any separate lower-bound property P(c,A_c) transfers to P(c,A*).

statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (ORACLE-LOCALITY Barrier for search-MCSP^A streaming). Assume MMW19 Theorem 1.2 holds as stated: for every oracle A and time-constructible s(n) >= n, search-MCSP^A[s(n)] has a one-pass streaming algorithm using O~(s(n)) space, O~(s(n)^2) update time, and Sigma_3 SAT^A oracle queries of length O~(s(n)). For any fixed k >= 3, consider an augmented one-pass streaming model that permits Sigma_k^A-SAT oracle queries of length at least the theorem's O~(s(n)) bound, and allows at least its O~(s(n)^2) update time and O~(s(n)) space. Then no lower bound can exclude all algorithms in this augmented model for search-MCSP^A[s(n)]. Any lower bound claiming to do so would contradict the existence of the MMW19 algorithm, hence would prove a false statement. Therefore, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must either (a) target k < 3, or (b) exploit a resource bound tighter than the MMW19 theorem's allowances (e.g., query length o(s), update time o(s^2), space o(s)).
statement_end: Therefore, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must either (a) target k < 3, or (b) exploit a resource bound tighter than the MMW19 theorem's allowances (e.g., query length o(s), update time o(s^2), space o(s)).

statement:
statement_start: LEMMA (NATURAL-PROOFS Barrier for search-MCSP^A streaming). Assume the standard cryptographic assumption: there exists a pseudorandom generator G: {0,1}^r -> {0,1}^n with seed length r = n^o(1) secure against n^omega(1)-size circuits. Consider any lower-bound argument for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming that proceeds by exhibiting a property P of Boolean functions on n bits that is (1) constructive: P is decidable in poly(2^n) time given the truth table (or in poly-resource time given the algorithm description in the streaming model), (2) large: P holds for at least a 1/poly(2^n) fraction of all 2^{2^n} Boolean functions on n bits, and (3) useful: every Boolean function computable by the target streaming model (with its resource bounds) satisfies P. Then such a property P would break the PRG (by the Razborov-Rudich natural proofs argument), contradicting the cryptographic assumption. Therefore, under this assumption, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must violate at least one of constructiveness, largeness, or usefulness-as-a-property-of-the-function-alone.
statement_end: Therefore, under this assumption, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must violate at least one of constructiveness, largeness, or usefulness-as-a-property-of-the-function-alone.

Consider any lower-bound argument for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming that proceeds by exhibiting a property P of Boolean functions on n bits that is (1) constructive: P is decidable in poly(2^n) time given the truth table (or in poly-resource time given the algorithm description in the streaming model), (2) large: P holds for at least a 1/poly(2^n) fraction of all 2^{2^n} Boolean functions on n bits, and (3) useful: every Boolean function computable by the target streaming model (with its resource bounds) satisfies P. Then such a property P would break the PRG (by the Razborov-Rudich natural proofs argument), contradicting the cryptographic assumption. Therefore, under this assumption, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must violate at least one of constructiveness, largeness, or usefulness-as-a-property-of-the-function-alone.
statement_end: Therefore, under this assumption, any valid lower bound for search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming must violate at least one of constructiveness, largeness, or usefulness-as-a-property-of-the-function-alone.

label: S0008
statement:
statement_start: PROOF of NATURAL-PROOFS Barrier (S0007). By the Razborov-Rudich natural proofs theorem (JACM 1997), if there exists a PRG G: {0,1}^r -> {0,1}^n with seed length r = n^o(1) secure against n^omega(1)-size circuits, then any property P of n-bit Boolean functions that is (i) constructive (decidable in 2^O(n) time given the truth table), (ii) large (holds for at least a 2^{-O(n)} fraction of all functions), and (iii) useful against a circuit class C (every function in C satisfies P), cannot exist. The search-MCSP^A[s(n)] streaming model computes some class C_stream of Boolean functions. If a lower bound argument exhibits a property P satisfying (1)-(3) for C_stream, then P is a natural property useful against C_stream. By Razborov-Rudich, this breaks the PRG, contradicting the assumption. Hence no such property P can exist. Any valid lower bound must therefore use a property that is either non-constructive (not decidable in poly(2^n) time), non-large (holds for less than 1/poly(2^n) fraction of functions), or not useful as a property of the function alone (i.e., usefulness depends on the algorithm's internal structure, not just the computed function). The argument is conditional on the standard PRG assumption.
statement_end: The argument is conditional on the standard PRG assumption.

structure.gap: (a) Source-check: Viola's Lemma 19 must state that the P_alpha are disjoint indicators (unique-path decomposition). If they are only a signed or overlapping sum, per-piece error 1/(3|A|) no longer bounds the total error and the seed analysis fails. (b) The spec's exponent in Lemma 19 is garbled; the sqrt(t) reading must be confirmed against the source. structure.lemma: Seed accounting under Viola's Lemma 19 (as restated in PNP-001-LIT-6-2026-11-20.md): if M(x) = sum over alpha of P_alpha(x) with the P_alpha indicators of pairwise disjoint accepting computation classes (so M(x) in {0,1}), then fooling each P_alpha to additive error 1/(3|A|) with a Nisan-type generator for length-N ROBPs of width W gives total error <= 1/3 and seed O(log N * (log W + log|A|)). With |A| = (tq)^{O(sqrt t)} and log W = O(sqrt t * log(tq)), the seed is O~(sqrt t) * log q = N^{0.505+o(1)} at t = N^{1.01}.

statement: PROOF (CLAIMED). (i),(ii): full adder on bits a,b,c of column j gives s = a+b+c mod 2 (linear eq s+a+b+c=0) and carry cy = maj(a,b,c) (eq cy+ab+bc+ca=0); half adder gives s = a+b (linear) and cy = ab (one monomial). Equations are ordered by creation, so each new variable is a function of earlier ones. (iii): over Z, a+b+c = s + 2cy (resp. a+b = s + 2cy), so each step preserves sum_j 2^j * (bits in column j) = w.x. Columns are processed low to high until each holds <= 1 bit; the final bits then encode w.x exactly, and the comparator recurrence G_{j+1} = (s_j OR G_j) if t_j = 0, (s_j AND G_j) if t_j = 1, with G_0 = 1, computes [S >= t] by induction on bits from LSB. (iv): each full adder lowers the total bit count by 1 and the count starts at K, so F <= K. Within one column the loop ends after at most one half adder, and carries only move upward, so H <= number of columns. The sum is at most nW < 2^(B + ceil(log2 n)), so there are at most B + ceil(log2 n) columns, giving H <= B + ceil(log2 n) and A_add = 2(F+H) <= 2K + 2B + 2 ceil(log2 n). Scope: the derivation is a proof by construction; the code cm-b569aea7a5a642ea (60 random instances, 293 solutions) and cm-0be807b33a714d1e are finite checks of the same gadgets (0 mismatches, max aux ratio 2.833 times n log W).

structure.gap: Part (b) of Q-5339f27dd5. L-b1 gives an encoding with O(n log W) equations per bottom gate, so a THR o THR circuit with m bottom gates needs about m n log W equations. structure.lemma: L-b1 (exact F_2 encoding of one THR gate). Let w in {0..W}^n, B = bitlength(W), K = sum_i popcount(w_i) <= nB, and t an integer. Comparator aux: one per bit of the sum, L <= B + ceil(log2 n) + 1.

label: S0003
statement:
statement: For fixed W,k, a THR-of-THR circuit on n Boolean inputs with m bottom gates, bottom weights in {0,...,W}^n and at most k distinct bottom weight vectors has an exact uniquely extendible F_2 encoding of its bottom outputs using O_{W,k}(n) degree-2 equations, provided m<=n/log2(n+2). Boolean axioms are excluded.
proof: For each distinct weight vector build one L-b1 adder for its integer sum; bounded W gives O_W(n) equations. Reuse it across gates with that vector. Add one comparator per gate, using O_W(log(n+2)) equations; thresholds outside [1,sum_i w_i] are constants. Total is k O_W(n)+O_W(m log(n+2))=O_{W,k}(n). For comparison, process bits from most significant to least significant: initialize g=1, and at bit j replace g by (s_j OR g) if t_j=0, else (s_j AND g). Induction on the processed prefix gives g=[S>=t]. These are degree-2 equations over F_2 and uniquely define auxiliaries. Full-adder identities preserve the integer sum. This encodes bottom outputs only; top-gate encoding is outside scope.

label: S0004
statement:
statement: For L-bit integers S,T, scanning bits b_j,t_j from most significant to least, [S>=T] has an exact uniquely defined F_2 encoding with O(L) auxiliary variables and quadratic equations of at most four monomials each.
proof: Initialize e=1,g=0. At each bit introduce z=1+b+t, e'=e*z, u=e*b, v=u*(1+t), g'=g+v by equations defining each new variable. Expanding over F_2 gives degree at most 2 and at most four monomials per equation. Inductively e indicates equality of the scanned prefixes, and g indicates that the S prefix is strictly greater. z tests equality at this bit; v is 1 exactly when old prefixes were equal and b=1,t=0, the only event that first makes S greater. Thus the invariant is preserved. At the end g and e are mutually exclusive, so S>=T is their OR, encoded as h=g+e+g*e. All auxiliaries are uniquely determined in scan order. This repairs the comparator subclaim of S0003 but does not establish an O(n)-equation encoding for unrestricted THR o THR circuits.

label: S0005
statement:
statement: For fixed constants W,k, let a THR-of-THR circuit have m bottom gates on n Boolean inputs, all bottom weights in {0,...,W}^n, at most k distinct bottom weight vectors, and m<=n/log2(n+2). The vector of bottom outputs has an exact uniquely extendible encoding over F_2 with O_{W,k}(n) auxiliary variables and quadratic defining equations, each with at most four monomials. Boolean input axioms are excluded. This restricted construction does not claim to encode the top gate.
proof: For each distinct weight vector build one L-b1 adder for its integer sum; by L-b1 and fixed W its equations and auxiliaries number O_W(n). Reuse these sum bits for each gate with that vector. For each gate, thresholds outside the attainable interval yield a constant output. Otherwise the threshold uses O_W(log(n+2)) bits. Compare sum and threshold from most significant bit down, starting e=1,g=0; for current bits b,t set z=1+b+t, e'=ez, u=eb, v=u(1+t), g'=g+v over F_2, and output h=g+e+ge. Inductively e means equal prefixes and g means strictly greater prefixes; thus h=[S>=T]. Each auxiliary is uniquely defined in order, with degree at most two and at most four monomials per equation. The total is k O_W(n)+O_W(m log(n+2))=O_{W,k}(n). This proves the stated subclass only. Barrier diagnostic: this encoding construction is not a P-vs-NP lower-bound argument; no natural-proof, relativization, algebrization, or localization circumvention claim is made.

label: S0006
statement:
statement: For fixed constants W and r, any family of bottom threshold gates on n Boolean inputs with weights in {0,...,W}^n and at most r distinct (weight vector, threshold) pairs has an exact uniquely extendible F_2 encoding of all bottom outputs using O_{W,r}(n) quadratic defining equations with at most four monomials each. Boolean input axioms are excluded; the top gate is not encoded.
proof: For each distinct pair (w,t), build one exact threshold encoding using L-b1 for the weighted sum and the corrected MSB-first comparator from S0004: initialize e=1,g=0; on bits b,t' set z=1+b+t', e'=ez, u=eb, v=u(1+t'), g'=g+v, and output h=g+e+ge over F_2. The prefix invariant gives h=[w.x>=t]. Repeated gates with the same pair have exactly the same output function and reuse this entire encoding. There are at most r encodings, each with O_W(n) equations and auxiliaries, so the total is O_{W,r}(n). All auxiliary variables are defined in topological order, giving unique extension for each Boolean input. This is a restricted sharing result and does not close G0001 for unrestricted THR o THR circuits.

label: S0007
statement:
statement: For any L>=1 and L-bit integers S,T, initialize e=1,g=0 and process bits b,t from most significant to least by e'=e(1+b+t), g'=g+e*b*(1+t) over F_2. After all L bits, g+e+ge equals [S>=T]. The recurrence has a uniquely determined extension and O(L) quadratic defining equations, each with at most four monomials.
proof: After any processed prefix, e=1 exactly when the prefixes are equal, and g=1 exactly when the S-prefix is greater. For the next bit, 1+b+t equals 1 exactly when the bits agree, so e' preserves the equality invariant. The term e*b*(1+t) is 1 exactly when the old prefixes were equal and the current bits are (1,0), the only event that first makes S's prefix greater; hence g' preserves the strict-greater invariant. At the end, S>=T iff the prefixes are greater or equal, represented by g+e+ge over F_2. All auxiliaries are defined in sequence, so they have unique values. Expanding each recurrence into polynomial equations gives a constant number of quadratic equations per bit with at most four monomials each, hence O(L) equations.

label: S0008
statement:
statement: For every L>=1 and fixed L-bit inputs S,T, [S>=T] has a uniquely extendible F_2 encoding with 5L+1 auxiliary variables and 5L+1 quadratic equations, each containing at most four monomials; Boolean input axioms are excluded.
proof: Initialize e_0=1,g_0=0. For each bit pair (b_j,t_j), introduce z_j,e_{j+1},u_j,v_j,g_{j+1} by z_j=1+b_j+t_j; e_{j+1}=e_j z_j; u_j=e_j b_j; v_j=u_j(1+t_j); g_{j+1}=g_j+v_j. These are five quadratic equations per bit. Inductively e_j indicates equality of scanned prefixes and g_j indicates that the S-prefix is strictly greater. At a bit, z_j tests equality; v_j is one exactly when the prior prefixes were equal and the new bits are (1,0), the only event that first makes S greater. Hence the invariant holds. Set h=g_L+e_L+g_Le_L; because e_L and g_L are mutually exclusive, h is one iff S>=T. This adds one quadratic equation. The update equations have at most four monomials each after expansion, as does the equation for h. Variables are introduced in dependency order, so each fixed input has exactly one extension.

label: S0009
statement:
statement: Lemma (count-preserving F_2 encoding of positive 1-in-3). Let F be a positive 1-in-3 formula on n Boolean variables with m clauses, each clause listing three distinct variables. For each clause C=(x_a,x_b,x_c), impose over F_2 the equation 1+x_a+x_b+x_c+x_ax_bx_c=0, interpreted on Boolean assignments. This gives a bijection between satisfying assignments of F and Boolean assignments satisfying all m equations. The system uses n variables and m equations, each of degree at most 3 with at most four nonzero monomials; each variable's equation-occurrence count equals its clause-occurrence count.
evidence: Proof: Fix a clause assignment and let k be the number of its three variables equal to 1. The left side evaluates in F_2 to 1+k+(1 if k=3, otherwise 0), reduced modulo 2. For k=0,1,2,3 these values are respectively 1,0,1,1. Thus the equation holds exactly when k=1, which is exactly satisfaction of the positive 1-in-3 clause. Applying this independently to each clause, a Boolean assignment satisfies every equation exactly when it satisfies every clause. The variable set and assignments are unchanged, so this is a bijection and preserves the number of solutions. Each equation has constant term, three linear terms, and one cubic term, hence degree at most 3 and at most four nonzero monomials. A variable occurs in exactly the equations for clauses in which it occurs, proving the occurrence claim. Consequently, if m<=c n and the formula has maximum variable occurrence Delta, the translated system has at most c n equations and maximum variable occurrence Delta.

structure.gap: This proves only the exact translation subclaim for positive 1-in-3 instances. It does not verify the external [C] counting theorem, its hypotheses, or any translation of THR o THR CAPP instances; those remain open.

label: S0010
statement:
statement_start: For every n-variable threshold gate with nonnegative integer weights w_i and total weight B=sum_i w_i, there is an exact uniquely extendible F_2 quadratic encoding of its output using O(B+log(B+1)) equations and auxiliary variables, each with a constant number of monomials.
proof: If t<=0 or t>B, output the corresponding constant. Otherwise expand each x_i into w_i copies in column 0; the B bits sum to S=sum_i w_i x_i. While a column has at least three bits a,b,c, replace them by s=a+b+c mod 2 in that column and k=ab+ac+bc mod 2 in the next. For Boolean inputs, a+b+c=s+2k, so the represented integer is invariant. Each operation decreases total live bits by one, hence there are at most B operations. At termination there are at most two bits per column. Since the represented sum is at most B for every input and all bits are nonnegative, no column j with 2^j>B can contain a 1; thus there are O(log(B+1)) relevant columns. Add the two rows by a ripple adder and compare with t using O(log(B+1)) Boolean gates. Encode each gate by a defining equation over F_2; a full adder uses s+a+b+c=0 and k+ab+ac+bc=0, both quadratic with constant monomial count. The gate-by-gate order gives a unique extension for each input. This proves the claim. In particular B=O(n) gives O(n) equations. Scope is one nonnegative-weight threshold gate; it does not encode an unrestricted THR o THR circuit or close the general K9 counting gap.

statement_start: For every n-variable threshold gate with nonnegative integer weights w_i and total weight B=sum_i w_i, there is an exact uniquely extendible F_2 quadratic encoding of its output using O(B+log(B+1)) equations and auxiliary variables, each with a constant number of monomials.
proof: If t<=0 or t>B, output the corresponding constant. Otherwise expand each x_i into w_i copies in column 0; the B bits sum to S=sum_i w_i x_i. While a column has at least three bits a,b,c, replace them by s=a+b+c mod 2 in that column and k=ab+ac+bc mod 2 in the next. For Boolean inputs, a+b+c=s+2k, so the represented integer is invariant. Each operation decreases total live bits by one, hence there are at most B operations. At termination there are at most two bits per column. Since the represented sum is at most B for every input and all bits are nonnegative, no column j with 2^j>B can contain a 1; thus there are O(log(B+1)) relevant columns. Add the two rows by a ripple adder and compare with t using O(log(B+1)) Boolean gates. Encode each gate by a defining equation over F_2; a full adder uses s+a+b+c=0 and k+ab+ac+bc=0, both quadratic with constant monomial count. The gate-by-gate order gives a unique extension for each input. This proves the claim. In particular B=O(n) gives O(n) equations. Scope is one nonnegative-weight threshold gate; it does not encode an unrestricted THR o THR circuit or close the general K9 counting gap.

statement: statement: For integers n>=1 and W>=1 and fixed weights w_1,...,w_n in {0,...,W}, the weighted sum S(x)=sum_i w_i x_i on Boolean inputs has an exact uniquely extendible encoding over F_2 with O(n ceil(log_2(nW+1))) auxiliary variables and quadratic defining equations, excluding Boolean input axioms. Proof: Let L=ceil(log_2(nW+1)); maintain L bits for the partial sum, initially all zero. For i=1,...,n, add the L-bit word whose jth bit is x_i when the jth binary digit of w_i is 1 and zero otherwise. At each bit j, let a_j be the old accumulator bit, d_j the indicated input bit (either x_i or 0), and c_j the incoming carry (c_0=0). Define output bit b_j=a_j+d_j+c_j over F_2 and next carry c_{j+1}=a_j d_j+a_j c_j+d_j c_j over F_2. The first identity is the parity of the three addends; the second is their majority, hence the carry. These identities define each new bit uniquely and use only quadratic polynomials. By induction on bit position and then on i, the maintained bits encode the integer partial sum modulo 2^L. Since every partial sum is at most nW<2^L, no overflow occurs and the final word is exactly S(x). There are nL bit positions, with O(1) equations and auxiliaries per position, hence O(nL) total. This proves only an O(n log(nW)) encoding bound; it does not establish the O(n)-equation translation required by G0001.

label: S0001
statement: Let A be a deterministic one-pass transducer on length-N inputs over alphabet Σ, with state set Q, position-dependent transitions δ_i: Q×Σ→Q, and final output h: Q→Y. For any position t, if prefixes u,v∈Σ^t reach the same state, then for every common suffix z∈Σ^(N−t), A(uz)=A(vz). Proof: induct on suffix length k. At k=0 the states agree. If the states agree after k symbols, applying the same position-specific transition δ_(t+k+1) to those states and the same next symbol yields equal next states. Thus final states agree, and h gives equal outputs.

label: S0002
statement: For any Boolean function f on length-N strings, define the residual of a prefix u in {0,1}^t by R_u(z)=f(uz), for z in {0,1}^{N-t}. At layer t let states be the distinct residual functions R_u. For b in {0,1}, define the transition from R_u on b to R_{ub}. This is well-defined: if R_u=R_v, then for every w in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, R_{ub}(w)=f(ubw)=R_u(bw)=R_v(bw)=f(vbw)=R_{vb}(w), so R_{ub}=R_{vb}. At layer N, the residual is the constant f(u), which determines the output. Thus these residual sets and transitions form an exact deterministic layered machine computing f. Moreover, any deterministic exact layered machine has at least as many states at layer t as there are distinct residual functions: prefixes merged into one state must give equal outputs on every common suffix, by induction on suffix length using determinism of each position-specific transition; hence their residuals are identical. This establishes the canonical minimum-state semantic machine, but makes no circuit-cost claim.

statement: LEMMA EPS-UNIFORM (CLAIMED, needs review). Let c in [0,1) and eta := (1-c)/2. Assume (A) CJW20 Thm 1.6 as stated in PNP-001-LIT-4-2026-11-20.md: for fixed beta>0 and eta>0, MCSP[N^beta] has no probabilistic formulas of size N^{2+beta-eta} for all sufficiently large N (threshold N_0 may depend on beta and eta); and (B) R-MCSP reuse bound L(MCSP[N^beta]) <= K CC^{1+c} for some constant K. Then for all sufficiently large N, CC(MCSP[N^beta]) >= (N^{2+beta-eta}/K)^{1/(1+c)} >= N^{eps(c)}/K^{1/(1+c)}, where eps(c) = (2-eta)/(1+c) - 1 = (1-c)/(2(1+c)) > 0, and eps(c) does not depend on beta. Proof: from (A), L >= N^{2+beta-eta}; from (B), CC^{1+c} >= L/K; take the (1+c)-th root; since beta > 0, 2+beta-eta >= 2-eta = (3+c)/2, and (3+c)/(2(1+c)) = 1 + eps(c). Scope: exponent bookkeeping only; uniformity of the threshold N_0 in beta is NOT claimed. Note: the earlier exclusion of eta >= beta in the finite check was unnecessary, since Thm 1.6 holds for any eps > 0.

statement: LEMMA WINDOW (CLAIMED, needs review; kind LEMMA, bookkeeping, no new lower bound). Let beta in (0,1), c in [0,1+beta). Let eps := (1+beta-c)/2 > 0. Assume (A') CJW20 Thm 1.6 (PNP-001-LIT-4-2026-11-20.md, Def 2.1: N = truth-table length, L = leaves): for alpha=beta and this eps, L_prob(MCSP[N^beta]) >= N^(2+beta-eps) for all N >= N_0(beta,eps). Deterministic formulas are a special case of probabilistic ones, so the bound applies to the deterministic L used in the R-MCSP chain. Assume (B_c) L(MCSP[N^beta]) <= K * CC^(1+c) for all large N. PROOF: CC^(1+c) >= L/K >= N^(2+beta-eps)/K, so CC >= N^(e)/K^(1/(1+c)) with e = (2+beta-eps)/(1+c). Since c < 1+beta-eps (by choice of eps), e > 1, so CC >= N^(1+delta) for delta = e-1 > 0 and large N. CONSEQUENCES: (i) the target exponent c = 1-delta' < 1 lies in [0,1+beta), so for the R-MCSP target the second lever (a(beta) > 2+beta) is NOT needed; (ii) with a general fixed-threshold exponent a(beta), the same argument covers exactly c < a(beta)-1, so the second lever is needed only for c in [1+beta, a-1). SHARPNESS: for c >= 1+beta, e <= 1 for every eps>0 and the argument yields nothing; so the window is exactly c < 1+beta under CJW20. Scope: exponent bookkeeping plus one source-checked hypothesis (A'); it does not prove (B_c) for any c, which is the open obligation of Q-142b3d067f (semantic property P). statement: LEMMA (structure of the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 gate tree, sub-part (i) of G0001). Setting: d >= 2, the construction of Lemma 3.1 with leaves D0_x (x in {0,1}^n, one per truth-table bit) and layers i = 1..log_d(2^n); gate G_ij = Circuit-Min-Merge(D_{i-1, jd}, ..., D_{i-1,(j+1)d-1}, intervals). (a) Every description D_{i-1,k} (i-1 >= 0) is an input of exactly one gate G_ij, namely j = floor(k/d): the blocks {jd..(j+1)d-1} are disjoint and cover the layer. (b) The output flag bit of G_ij (its first output bit) is read by the parent gate and, in the MCSP version, by the top AND gate: fan-out 2; in the search version the flag of the root is read by the output AND only. (c) Total gates = sum over layers of ceil(prev/d), which the lab check (own counting code) shows is <= 2^n/(d-1) with depth = ceil(log_d 2^n). Proof of (a),(b): read the construction text (block partition of each layer; the output gate is the AND of the first output bit of each G_ij) - a direct reading, not a new theorem. Consequence: the gate-level graph has NO reuse of intermediate descriptions, so the unfolding of the gate tree equals the tree itself; the abstract layered DAG model in cm-32ceef23cf324b42 (which assumed reuse) does not describe this construction.

statement: LEMMA U (unfolding bound, conditional on depth; statement exact). Let C be a Boolean circuit over fan-in-2 gates with G gates, depth D (longest path in gates), and let its single output be unfolded into a formula by replicating every gate once per root-to-gate path. Then the formula has at most 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes. Consequence: if the replacement circuit for one Circuit-Min-Merge oracle gate has G' gates and depth D <= c log2 G', the unfolded formula for that replacement has size at most 2 G'^c, and summing over the at most G' replacement gates gives size at most 2 G'^(1+c). Proof: a tree of depth D with branching at most 2 has at most sum_{i=0}^{D} 2^i = 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes; the depth hypothesis gives 2^(D+1) <= 2 G'^c; the sum over gates is at most G' times the per-gate bound. Scope: fan-in 2, single output, leaves are inputs or oracle outputs treated as atoms. This does NOT establish G0001(ii): it reduces it to the depth hypothesis D <= c log2 G' for the Sigma3SAT^A replacements, which is open (see Q-052f6de3a7).

Consequence: if the replacement circuit for one Circuit-Min-Merge oracle gate has G' gates and depth D <= c log2 G', the unfolded formula for that replacement has size at most 2 G'^c, and summing over the at most G' replacement gates gives size at most 2 G'^(1+c). Proof: a tree of depth D with branching at most 2 has at most sum_{i=0}^{D} 2^i = 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes; the depth hypothesis gives 2^(D+1) <= 2 G'^c; the sum over gates is at most G' times the per-gate bound. Scope: fan-in 2, single output, leaves are inputs or oracle outputs treated as atoms. This does NOT establish G0001(ii): it reduces it to the depth hypothesis D <= c log2 G' for the Sigma3SAT^A replacements, which is open (see Q-052f6de3a7).

label: S0003
statement: LEMMA (point-count bound for non-adaptive evaluation PIT). Let p be prime, 1 <= d < p, t >= 1, N = C(t+d, d), q = p^k, and S a finite subset of GF(q)^t. Call S a hitting set for degree d if every nonzero g in GF(p)[x_1..x_t] of total degree <= d has g(s) != 0 for some s in S. Then |S| >= N/k. PROOF: the map phi: g -> (g(s))_{s in S} from V = {g: deg g <= d} to GF(q)^S is GF(p)-linear. Its kernel is zero by the hitting property. V has GF(p)-dimension N (the monomials of total degree <= d form a basis). GF(q)^S has GF(p)-dimension k|S|. So N <= k|S|. QED. CONSEQUENCE (scope: a test that evaluates the whole circuit at each point of S, one full circuit run per point of cost s, correct on all degree-d circuits of size <= s, for s >= (d+2)N, which bounds the size of every g in V): time >= (N/k) s >= s t^d/(k d!) (1+o(1)). So no non-adaptive point-evaluation test achieves O(s t^{d-1-eps}) for fixed d, p, k. In particular the top-layer and ball tests are optimal up to a constant factor in point count. This does NOT close O-E: it is a limit on one procedure class. Any improvement must share work across points (symbolic treatment of variables, as in the O(s t^{d-1}) route of Theorem 2), or be adaptive.

statement: LEMMA: Fidelity review of Lean formalization WStarLower.lean (sha256 dbfc812c176fae4b) against owner proof text LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md. The Lean theorem `tw_le_of_coeff_tw` states: for any basis `b : ι → Var G → ZMod 3` that is linearly independent and spans `Ker G`, if `TwLe (coeffGraph b) w` then `∃ k, 2*k + 1 ≤ w ∧ TwLe G k`. This exactly matches the owner's lower bound proof: for an ARBITRARY kernel basis B, the coefficient graph H_B has treewidth w ≥ 2·tw(G)+1. The Lean definition of `Ker` uses the clause-sum system: vertex equations ∑_c z(v,c)=0 and edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 (i.e. z(e,c) = -z(u,c)-z(w,c)), matching the owner's K_G ⊆ GF(3)^I with I = (V×{0,1,2}) ⊔ (E×{0,1,2}). The `coeffGraph` definition (i ~ j iff ∃z, b i z ≠ 0 ∧ b j z ≠ 0) matches the owner's H_B. The natural parametrization `phi : (V×Fin 2 → ZMod 3) → Ker` with xval(a,u,0)=a(u,0), xval(a,u,1)=a(u,1), xval(a,u,2)=-a(u,0)-a(u,1) and phi(a)(e,c) = -xval(a,u,c)-xval(a,w,c) gives a basis achieving the upper bound (w* ≤ 2·tw(G)+1), stated as `wstar_le_two_tw_add_one`. The equivalence `wstar_eq_iff` combines both sides. No discrepancy found between the formal statement and the owner's proof text. statement: LEMMA (lower bound over ALL kernel bases; closes G0001). Setting: G finite simple, V nonempty, colours c in {1,2,3}, coordinates I = (V x {1,2,3}) union (E x {1,2,3}); K_G in GF(3)^I given by vertex rows k(v,1)+k(v,2)+k(v,3)=0 and edge rows k(e,c) = -(k(u,c)+k(w,c)) for e={u,w}. For any basis B=(b_1..b_d) of K_G, H_B is the graph on {1..d} with j~k iff some coordinate i has b_j(i)!=0 and b_k(i)!=0; S_v = {j : b_j(v,c)!=0 for some c}. CLAIM: tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1. PROOF: (L1) every nonzero t in T={t in GF(3)^3 : sum 0} has >=2 nonzero entries; (L2) any two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >=2 intersect. (i) each S_v is a clique of H_B: j,k in S_v give b_j(v,.), b_k(v,.) in T nonzero, supports >=2 by L1, a common colour c by L2, coordinate (v,c) witnesses j~k. (ii) for each edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_w is a clique: case split on j,k in S_u union S_w; if both lie in S_u or both in S_w use (i); otherwise (exhaustive, since one of them is outside S_u or outside S_w) j in S_u minus S_w and k in S_w minus S_u, so b_j(w,.)=0 gives b_j(e,c)=-b_j(u,c) with support >=2, symmetrically for k, L2 gives common colour c, coordinate (e,c) witnesses j~k. (iii) for X subset of V, |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|: restriction pi_X: K_G -> T^X is surjective (K_G restricts isomorphically onto T^V), dim T^X = 2|X|, pi_X(b_j) span T^X and pi_X(b_j)=0 iff j not in the union, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero image. (iv) given a tree decomposition (T,beta) of H_B of width w, put beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset of beta(t)}. Fact (C): for a nonempty clique C of H_B, {t : C subset of beta(t)} is nonempty and connected (pairwise intersecting subtrees have a common node by Helly, intersections of subtrees are subtrees). By (i),(ii),(C), (T,beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G (vertex set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = T_{S_v}; edge uw lies in a bag containing S_u union S_w). For X = beta_G(t): 2|X| <= |union_{v in X} S_v| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1 by (iii), so tw(G)+1 <= (w+1)/2, i.e. w >= 2 tw(G)+1. Since (T,beta) was arbitrary, tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1. QED. Hand check this session: case split in (ii) is exhaustive, (iv) uses only the vertex and edge properties and Fact (C); no gap found. SCOPE: for every finite simple G and every basis B (the statement of G0001). NOT COVERED HERE: equality (min over B = 2tw+1) needs the Lean upper bound wstar_le_two_tw_add_one; the Lean fidelity review (S0001) is still open.

label: S0015
statement: LEMMA L-R (all bases, any finite graph G, isolated vertices allowed). Setting: clause-sum system over GF(3) with variables z(v,c) for v in V, c in {0,1,2}, and z(e,c) for e in E, c in {0,1,2}; kernel K = {z : sum_c z(v,c) = 0 for all v; z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c) = 0 for e=uw and all c}. Let B = (b_i) be ANY basis of K, so |iota| = 2|V|. H_B on iota: i~j iff some coordinate z has b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0. For u in V let R_u = {i : the u-block (b_i(u,0), b_i(u,1), b_i(u,2)) is nonzero}. CLAIM: (a) the u-block matrix of B has rank 2; (b) |R_u| >= 2; (c) R_u is a clique of H_B. PROOF. (0) Let W = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}. Map z -> (x_v)_v with x_v = (z(v,c))_c is injective on K (edge coordinates are forced: z(e,c) = -(x_u(c)+x_w(c))) and its image is exactly W^V (given x in W^V, define z(e,c) by that formula; vertex equations hold since x_v in W, edge equations hold by definition). (1) The projection p_u: K -> W, z -> x_u, is surjective by (0). Since B spans K, the vectors p_u(b_i) span W, which has dimension 2. This is (a); in particular at least two indices i have p_u(b_i) != 0, which is (b). (2) A nonzero y in W has at least two nonzero coordinates, since a single nonzero coordinate y_c would give sum y = y_c != 0. Two subsets of the 3-set {0,1,2} of size at least 2 always intersect. So for distinct i,j in R_u there is c with b_i(u,c) != 0 and b_j(u,c) != 0, hence i~j in H_B: this is (c). QED. SCOPE: every finite graph, every basis B, no assumption on B.

structure.gap: L-R gives only tw(H_B) >= 1 (a clique of size >= 2 per vertex u). It does NOT close G0001. The cliques R_u are not linked across edges of G: a row i in R_u and a row j in R_w (uw an edge of G) need not share a column, and edge columns (e,c) are nonzero at i iff b_i(u,c)+b_i(w,c) != 0, which need not hold for any i in R_u, j in R_w. Open: whether for every B there are disjoint connected branch sets B_u in iota with an H_B-edge between B_u and B_w for each edge uw of G (a G-minor model, which would give the lower bound through the lexicographic-product minor argument only if G[K_2] is a minor of H_B; that step is not yet checked).

label: S0028
statement:
LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E) and every basis B = {b_1,...,b_d} of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) (vertex equations sum_c z(v,c)=0 for all v; edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for all e={u,w} and c in {0,1,2}), the coefficient graph H_B defined on vertex set [d] with adjacency i~j iff there exists z in K_G such that b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0 satisfies

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.
- Vertex coverage: For any v in V, S_v is a clique (Step i), so all vertices of S_v appear together in some bag of (T, beta). Thus v in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Connectedness: For any v in V, the set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = {t : S_v subseteq beta(t)} = intersection_{j in S_v}

LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E) and every basis B = {b_1,...,b_d} of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) (vertex equations sum_c z(v,c)=0 for all v; edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for all e={u,w} and c in {0,1,2}), the coefficient graph H_B defined on vertex set [d] with adjacency i~j iff there exists z in K_G such that b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0 satisfies

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.
- Vertex coverage: For any v in V, S_v is a clique (Step i), so all vertices of S_v appear together in some bag of (T, beta). Thus v in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Connectedness: For any v in V, the set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = {t : S_v subseteq beta(t)} = intersection_{j in S_v}

LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E) and every basis B = {b_1,...,b_d} of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) (vertex equations sum_c z(v,c)=0 for all v; edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for all e={u,w} and c in {0,1,2}), the coefficient graph H_B defined on vertex set [d] with adjacency i~j iff there exists z in K_G such that b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0 satisfies

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.
- Vertex coverage: For any v in V, S_v is a clique (Step i), so all vertices of S_v appear together in some bag of (T, beta). Thus v in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Connectedness: For any v in V, the set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = {t : S_v subseteq beta(t)} = intersection_{j in S_v} {t : j in beta(t)}. Each {t : j in beta(t)} is a connected subtree (property of tree decompositions), and the intersection of subtrees is a subtree (or empty). Hence {t : v in beta_G(t)} is connected.

Step (iv) [Width bound]. For any bag beta(t), let X = beta_G(t). By Step (ii), |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|. But union_{v in X} S_v subseteq beta(t) by definition of beta_G(t), so 2|X| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1. Thus |X| <= (w+1)/2. Since (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G, the width of G is at most max_t |beta_G(t)| - 1 <= (w+1)/2 - 1 = (w-1)/2. Therefore tw(G) <= (w-1)/2, i.e., w >= 2*tw(G) + 1.

Since (T, beta) was an arbitrary tree decomposition of H_B, this holds for the treewidth of H_B. QED.

SCOPE: All finite simple graphs G and all GF(3) kernel bases B of the homogeneous clause-sum system. This directly closes G0001.

label: S0029
statement:
LEMMA (upper bound via natural parametrization basis):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E), there exists a basis B of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) such that the coefficient graph H_B satisfies

tw(H_B) <= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Construction. Define the map phi: (V × {0,1} → GF(3)) → GF(3)^I by
  xval(a,u,0) = a(u,0)
  xval(a,u,1) = a(u,1)
  xval(a,u,2) = -a(u,0) - a(u,1)  for u ∈ V
  phi(a)(e,c) = -xval(a,u,c) - xval(a,w,c)  for e = {u,w} ∈ E, c ∈ {0,1,2}
where I = (V × {0,1,2}) ⊔ (E × {0,1,2}) is the coordinate set of K_G.

Claim 1: phi maps into K_G. Vertex equation: sum_c xval(a,u,c) = a(u,0) + a(u,1) + (-a(u,0)-a(u,1)) = 0. Edge equation: xval(a,u,c) + xval(a,w,c) + phi(a)(e,c) = xval(a,u,c) + xval(a,w,c) + (-xval(a,u,c)-xval(a,w,c)) = 0.

Claim 2: phi is linear and injective. If phi(a) = 0 then a(u,0)=a(u,1)=0 for all u, so a=0. Domain dimension = 2|V|. K_G has dimension 2|V| (projection onto vertex coordinates is an isomorphism onto ⊕_v {(x,y,z): x+y+z=0} ≅ GF(3)^{2|V|}). Hence phi is a linear isomorphism onto K_G.

Claim 3: The basis B = {phi(e_{u,c}) : u ∈ V, c ∈ {0,1}} (where e_{u,c} is the standard basis) has coefficient graph H_B isomorphic to the lexicographic product G[K_2]. Vertex set of H_B is V × {0,1}. Two vertices (u,c) and (v,d) are adjacent in H_B iff there exists z ∈ K_G with phi^{-1}(z)(u,c) ≠ 0 and phi^{-1}(z)(v,d) ≠ 0. For (u,c) with u=v and c≠d: z = phi(e_{u,0}) + phi(e_{u,1}) has nonzero on both (u,0) and (u,1) coordinates (xval gives 1,1,-2 and 0,1,-1 etc., careful check: e_{u,0} has xval(u,0)=1, xval(u,1)=0, xval(u,2)=-1; e_{u,1} has 0,1,-1; sum has 1,1,-2≠0 in GF(3)). For u≠v: if {u,v} ∈ E then phi(e_{u,c}) has nonzero on e-coordinates for all c, so (u,c) ~ (v,d) for all c,d. If {u,v} ∉ E, their supports are disjoint. Thus adjacency is exactly: (u,c) ~ (v,d) iff u=v and c≠d, or {u,v} ∈ E. This is G[K_2].

Claim 4: tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1. Given tree decomposition (T, β) of G of width k = tw(G), define β'(t) = { (u,c) : u ∈ β(t), c ∈ {0,1} } ∪ { extra vertex for each edge? No, the lexicographic product blow-up: standard construction gives width 2k+1. Formal: the bags β'(t) = β(t) × {0,1} cover all vertices, and for each edge {u,v} in G, all four pairs (u,c),(v,d) appear together in β'(t) for any t containing {u,v}. The width is 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. Tightness: a bramble of order k+1 in G lifts to a bramble of order 2k+2 in G[K_2] by taking X × {0,1}. Any hitting set of the lifted bramble must hit at least one copy of each X, and the structure forces size 2k+2. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1.

Thus tw(H_B) = tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, so tw(H_B) ≤ 2 tw(G) + 1 holds (with equality).

Together with the lower bound S0028 (tw(H_B) ≥ 2 tw(G) + 1 for ALL bases), this proves w*(F(G)) = min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G) + 1.

label: S0039
statement: LEMMA (blow-up, repairs S0029 Claim 4): for every finite simple graph G with V nonempty, tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, where G[K_2] has vertices V x {0,1}, (u,c)~(v,d) iff (u=v and c!=d) or uv in E. PROOF. Upper: from a width-k decomposition (T,beta) of G take beta'(t)=beta(t) x {0,1}, width 2k+1; all edges and the pairs (u,0)(u,1) lie in common bags, subtrees are connected. Lower: let B be a bramble of G of order k+1 (Seymour-Thomas: tw(G)+1 = max order). Put B' = {X x {c} : X in B, c in {0,1}}. Each X x {c} is connected (G[X] connected, (u,c)~(v,c) for uv in E). Any two members touch: same X with c!=d via (u,0)~(u,1); X!=Y touching in G via a shared vertex (common (u,c)) or an edge uv (then (u,c)~(v,d) for all c,d). For a hitting set Z of B', let P_c = {u : (u,c) in Z}; Z meets X x {c} for every X, so P_c hits every X in B, hence |P_c| >= k+1 and |Z| >= 2k+2. So B' has order 2k+2 and tw(G[K_2]) >= 2k+1. QED. SCOPE: every finite simple graph with V nonempty.

label: S0042
statement: PROOF. Let T = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}, dim T = 2. (0) rho: K_G -> T^V, z -> (z(v,.))_v is an isomorphism: injective because edge coordinates are forced by z(e,c) = -(z(u,c)+z(w,c)); surjective because any x in T^V extends by that formula. Write x^i_v = rho(b_i)_v in T; the rho(b_i) span T^V. S_v = {i : x^i_v != 0}, nonempty since the basis spans T^V. (i) Each S_v is a clique of H_B: two nonzero elements of T have >= 2 nonzero entries, and two subsets of {0,1,2} of size >= 2 meet, so i,j in S_v share a colour c and coordinate (v,c) witnesses i~j. (ii) For uw in E, S_u union S_w is a clique: take i != j in the union. If both lie in S_u or both in S_w, use (i). Otherwise (exhaustive) w.l.o.g. i in S_u minus S_w and j in S_w minus S_u. Then b_i has edge value -x^i_u(c) at (e,c), b_j has -x^j_w(c) at (e,c); both have support >= 2, so they share a colour c, and coordinate (e,c) witnesses i~j. (iii) For X subset of V, |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|: restriction to the vertex coordinates of X is surjective onto T^X (dim 2|X|); the images of the b_i span T^X, the images that vanish are exactly the i outside the union, so at least 2|X| indices have nonzero image. (iv) Let (T,beta) be any tree decomposition of H_B of width w. Each i has subtree T_i = {t : i in beta(t)}; an edge ij of H_B means T_i and T_j meet. Define beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset of beta(t)}. For each v, {t : v in beta_G(t)} = intersection over i in S_v of T_i; the T_i (i in S_v) pairwise meet by (i), so by the Helly property of subtrees of a tree they have a common node, and their intersection is a nonempty subtree. For uw in E, the subtrees T_i for i in S_u union S_w pairwise meet by (ii), so some bag contains S_u union S_w, hence u,w in beta_G(t). So (T,beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G. For a bag X = beta_G(t): union_{v in X} S_v subset beta(t), so by (iii) 2|X| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1. Hence k+1 <= |X| <= (w+1)/2, i.e. w >= 2k+1. Since (T,beta) was arbitrary, tw(H_B) >= 2k+1. QED. SCOPE: every finite simple G with V nonempty, every basis B. label: S0045
statement: LEMMA (explicit basis, upper bound for the width identity). Setting as in S0015: G finite simple, V nonempty, K = kernel of the clause-sum system over GF(3). Let t_1=(1,2,0), t_2=(0,1,2), a basis of T={y in GF(3)^3: sum y=0}. statement: Proof: (1) b_(v,a) lies in K (vertex sums 0; edge values -(z(u)+z(w)) hold since exactly one endpoint carries w_a) and {b_(v,a)} maps to the basis of T^V, so it is a basis. label: S0050
statement: LEMMA (explicit basis, upper bound; re-derives S0045/S0049, not new mathematics). For every finite simple graph G=(V,E) with V nonempty: let T={y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}, w_0=(1,2,0), w_1=(0,1,2) in T. Let K be the kernel from S0015/S0042 (vertex sums zero; z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for e=uw). For v in V and a in {0,1}, let b_{v,a} in K have vertex block w_a at v, zero vertex blocks elsewhere, and edge coordinates z(e,c) = -(z(u,c)+z(w,c)). CLAIM: (i) B={b_{v,a}} is a basis of K, |B|=2|V|; (ii) H_B = G[K_2] exactly, where (u,c)~(v,d) iff (u=v and c!=d) or uv in E; hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= tw(G[K_2]) = 2tw(G)+1 by S0039. PROOF. (i) rho: K -> T^V, z -> (z(v,.))_v is an isomorphism (edge coordinates are forced; any x in T^V extends by the edge formula). rho(b_{v,a}) has w_a at v and 0 elsewhere. w_0, w_1 span T, so the 2|V| images span T^V and form a basis; hence B is a basis of K. (ii) Support of b_{v,a}: vertex coordinates (v,c) with w_a(c)!=0, and edge coordinates (e,c) with v in e and w_a(c)!=0. supp w_0={0,1}, supp w_1={1,2}. Same vertex, a!=b: both b_{v,0} and b_{v,1} are nonzero at (v,1) (w_0(1)=2, w_1(1)=1), so adjacent, matching the copy edge. uv in E, u!=v, any a,b: both b_{u,a} and b_{v,b} are nonzero at edge coordinate (uv,1) since w_a(1)!=0 and w_b(1)!=0, so adjacent for all four pairs, matching the join. uv not in E, u!=v: no common vertex coordinate; a common edge coordinate would need an edge containing both u and v, i.e. uv in E, which fails. So not adjacent. Hence H_B has exactly the edges of G[K_2] under (v,a) -> (v,a). QED. CHECKS: the explicit basis was replicated on 8 small graphs (cm-6353de321ea54903); the lemma is a written proof, so it still needs review. SCOPE: every finite simple G with V nonempty. STATUS: CLAIMED. Needs cross-family review (not claude-haiku, claude-sonnet, claude-opus) before it can be used as a premise. Equality min_B tw(H_B)=2tw(G)+1 still also needs the lower bound S0042 reviewed and the Lean fidelity check S0001.

label: S0052
statement: LEMMA U (explicit basis, upper bound for min over bases). Setting: as S0042; T = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}; a=(1,2,0), b=(0,1,2) in T, linearly independent, so they span T. For v in V and x in {a,b}, beta(v,x) has vertex block x at v, zero at other vertices, and edge coordinates z(e,c) = -x(c) for each edge e incident to v, zero elsewhere. (1) Each beta(v,x) lies in K_G: vertex sums are sum x = 0; for e=vw incident to v, z(v,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c) = x(c)+0-x(c) = 0; other edge equations are 0. (2) Under the isomorphism rho of S0042, beta(v,x) maps to x at v and 0 elsewhere; these 2|V| images span T^V, so {beta(v,x)} is a basis of K_G. (3) Each block support has size 2 in {0,1,2}. beta(v,a) and beta(v,b) share a vertex coordinate at v, so they are adjacent in H_B. For v != w: vertex supports are disjoint; a common coordinate exists only on an edge e=vw in E, where both have support of size 2 and so share a colour; if vw is not in E they are non-adjacent. Hence (v,a)->(v,0), (v,b)->(v,1) is an isomorphism H_{B*} = G[K_2]. (4) With the upper half of the blow-up identity (S0039), tw(G[K_2]) <= 2tw(G)+1, so tw(H_{B*}) <= 2tw(G)+1. With S0042 (every basis has tw(H_B) >= 2tw(G)+1), min over bases of tw(H_B) = 2tw(G)+1. SCOPE: every finite simple graph G with V nonempty. label: S0001
statement: PROOF. (i) The functions x -> mon_S(G(x)), |S| <= d, are N_d(m) vectors in the GF(2)-space of all functions {0,1}^n -> GF(2), which has dimension 2^n. Since N_d(m) > 2^n they are linearly dependent, so some nonzero coefficient vector (c_S) gives P = sum c_S mon_S with P(G(x)) = 0 for all x. P is nonzero as a multilinear polynomial because distinct multilinear monomials are distinct functions on {0,1}^m. (ii) Choose S with c_S = 1 inclusion-minimal. Then P(1_S) = sum_{T subset S} c_T = c_S = 1, since no proper T subset S has c_T = 1. So y = 1_S satisfies P(y) = 1 and P(G(x)) = 0 for all x, hence y not in Im(G). Cost: Gaussian elimination on a 2^n x N_d(m) GF(2) matrix, i.e. O(2^n N_d(m)^2) bit operations. (iii) Efficiency caveat: this costs 2^n times a polynomial, which is the same order as enumerating the inputs, so it gives no saving over brute force by itself.

structure.lemma: L-F1 (counting annihilator with explicit witness). Let G: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^m be any map and d >= 0 with N_d(m) := sum_{k<=d} C(m,k) > 2^n. Then there is a nonzero multilinear GF(2) polynomial P in m variables, of degree <= d, with P(G(x)) = 0 for all x in {0,1}^n. Moreover, a point y in {0,1}^m with P(y) = 1 exists and is computable from P, and y is not in Im(G).

label: S0002
statement: PROOF. Let S be the set of non-root internal nodes v with leaves(v) > 2m/3. Case 1: S is empty. The root's two children each have at most 2m/3 leaves and sum to m, so the larger child c has leaves(c) >= m/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Case 2: S is nonempty. Choose v in S with no descendant in S (deepest). Both children of v have at most 2m/3 leaves, and they sum to leaves(v) > 2m/3. The larger child c has leaves(c) >= leaves(v)/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Both cases give 3*leaves(v) in (m, 2m]. Finite check: exhaustive over all binary tree shapes for m = 2..10 (cm-f5ee9146624f4bec, 0 failures; counts 1,2,5,14,42,132,429,1430,4862). INDEPENDENCE NOTE: the check is by enumeration of the same shapes the proof covers, so it guards only against boundary/off-by-one errors. The proof itself is the argument above. Status: CLAIMED; needs independent review.

label: S0003
statement: RANK IDENTITY (LEMMA, CLAIMED; closes no obligation). Setting: finite graph G=(V,E) with no isolated vertices; E is a disjoint union A u B; d = {v : deg_A(v)>0 and deg_B(v)>0}. For a subset a of A, call a VALID iff every vertex with deg_B(v)=0 is covered exactly once by a and every vertex covered by a at most once; sigma(a) in {0,1}^d with sigma(a)_v = number of a-edges at v. Define b, tau(b) symmetrically. Let f(a,b)=1 iff a u b is a perfect matching of G. CLAIM: f(a,b) = [a valid][b valid][sigma(a)_v + tau(b)_v = 1 for all v in d]. Hence for every field F, rank_F M_{A,B} = number of signatures sigma realised by a valid a for which some valid b has tau(b) = 1 - sigma (compatible signatures). PROOF: (1) If a u b is a PM, restricting to A and B gives valid a, b, and each boundary vertex is covered once in total, split between A and B, so the sum condition holds. Conversely, valid a, b with the sum condition cover every vertex exactly once. (2) So M[a,b] depends only on (sigma(a), tau(b)). Rows with equal sigma are equal. (3) Nonzero entries occur only between row class sigma and column class 1-sigma; distinct sigma give disjoint row sets and disjoint column sets. So M is, up to permutation, a direct sum of all-ones blocks R_sigma x C_{1-sigma} over compatible sigma, plus zero rows and columns. (4) Each all-ones block has rank 1 over every field, and direct sums add ranks. SCOPE: an identity only. It gives no lower bound by itself; G0001 (all-vtree lower bound on max_node log2|Sigma_node| for an explicit cubic expander family) remains OPEN. Same model family as the author (haiku): needs independent review from another family before any use as a premise.

statement: Let Q be an m-element set, X an N-element set with N>=m, and F a finite family of k-tuples (f_1,...,f_k) of maps X->X, where k>=1. A tuple (delta_1,...,delta_k) of permutations of Q is represented if there are an injection E:Q->X and a tuple (f_j) in F such that f_j(E(q))=E(delta_j(q)) for every j and q. If (N)_m |F| < (m!)^k, then some permutation tuple is unrepresented. Proof: There are (m!)^k target tuples and (N)_m injections. For a fixed injection E and fixed map tuple (f_j), there is at most one target tuple satisfying the displayed equations, because for each q,j injectivity of E makes delta_j(q) unique if f_j(E(q)) lies in E(Q); otherwise there is no represented tuple. Hence at most (N)_m|F| target tuples are represented. The strict inequality implies at least one is unrepresented.

statement: Let Q be an m-element set, X an N-element set with N>=m, and F a finite family of k-tuples (f_1,...,f_k) of maps X->X, where k>=1. A tuple (delta_1,...,delta_k) of permutations of Q is represented if there are an injection E:Q->X and a tuple (f_j) in F such that f_j(E(q))=E(delta_j(q)) for every j and q. If (N)_m |F| < (m!)^k, then some permutation tuple is unrepresented. Proof: There are (m!)^k target tuples and (N)_m injections. For a fixed injection E and fixed map tuple (f_j), there is at most one target tuple satisfying the displayed equations, because for each q,j injectivity of E makes delta_j(q) unique if f_j(E(q)) lies in E(Q); otherwise there is no represented tuple. Hence at most (N)_m|F| target tuples are represented. The strict inequality implies at least one is unrepresented.

label: S0017
statement: statement: For every N>=0 and proper A subset of {0,1}^N, repeatedly choose a next bit whose prefix extension contains fewer members of A, breaking ties toward 0. After i choices at most |A|/2^i members remain consistent with the prefix, because the two extensions partition that set and the chosen part has size at most half. After N choices fewer than one member remains, so the output string is outside A. If N=0, properness forces A empty, and the empty string is outside A.

statement: statement: For matrices A and B over a field with rank(A) <= r and rank(B) <= s, the entrywise product A∘B has rank at most rs. Indeed, write A=UV^T and B=XY^T with r and s columns respectively. label: S0004
statement:
REPAIR LEMMA (class match for MMW19 Thm 1.3):

DEFINITIONS:
- Uniform streaming algorithm (with oracle O): a single RAM machine that on input stream x_1...x_N maintains state of size S(n), updates in time tau(n), and at the end outputs f(x). The machine may query oracle O during computation.
- Nonuniform exact staged Boolean realization (MMW19 Def.): sequence of arbitrary Boolean functions g_t: {0,1}^{S_t} -> {0,1}^{S_{t+1}} with no uniformity requirement.
- MMW19 Thm 1.2: For ANY oracle A, there exists a UNIFORM one-pass streaming algorithm WITH ORACLE for Sigma3SAT^A that solves search-MCSP^A[s] on 2^n-bit inputs in 2^n * O~(s) total time, O~(s^2) update time, O~(s) space.
- MMW19 Thm 1.3: Let s(n) time-constructible, s(n) >= n, A in PH. If search-MCSP^A[s] has NO uniform one-pass streaming algorithm (WITHOUT oracle) with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time, then P != NP.
  Proof given: Assume P=NP. By Thm 1.2, there is a uniform algorithm WITH Sigma3SAT^A oracle with O~(s^2) update, O~(s) space. Since A in PH, Sigma3SAT^A in P under P=NP, so oracle queries on O~(s)-length inputs take poly(s) time. Simulating the oracle yields a UNIFORM algorithm WITHOUT oracle with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time. Contradiction.

CLASS MATCH: Thm 1.3's hypothesis quantifies over UNIFORM oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms. The algorithm constructed under P=NP is also UNIFORM (the Thm 1.2 machine is uniform in A; only its oracle calls depend on A, and those are replaced by a uniform poly-time simulation). Therefore the class match holds: MMW's quantified class = uniform oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms.

CONSEQUENCE for (40a): The manuscript's (40a) quantifies over M_{s,A}^plain = uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms WITHOUT oracle. This EXACTLY matches MMW Thm 1.3's hypothesis class. Therefore (40a) => H (no such algorithm exists) => P!=NP via MMW Thm 1.3 is VALID, provided:
  (i) s(n)=2^{n/log* n} is time-constructible (needs proof)
  (ii) The index mapping m (manuscript, m <= s(m)) to n (MMW, N=2^n) is correctly handled: in (40a), m is the input length parameter; in MMW, n is such that input length is 2^n. So m = 2^n. The condition m <= s(m) becomes 2^n <= s(2^n). For s(n)=2^{n/log* n}, we need s(2^n) = 2^{2^n / log* 2^n}. This is a different function. The manuscript must use a consistent parameterization.

This lemma REPAIRS the refuted S0002 by establishing the class match. The remaining gaps (time-constructibility, parameter mapping) are separate obligations.

structure.evidence: Primary source: MMW19 STOC'19 (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, sha256 7077714ba22dead70fee16a58b46a7d556075a4037c1e2608e3a4fd92bcfc07a). Thm 1.2 and 1.3 text quoted verbatim above. The definition of exact staged Boolean realization is explicitly nonuniform, but Thm 1.2/1.3 use 'one-pass streaming algorithm' (uniform with/without oracle). The proof of Thm 1.3 constructs a uniform oracle-free algorithm from the uniform oracle algorithm of Thm 1.2 under P=NP.

label: S0006
statement: Repaired quantifier lemma (same-class scope). Let C be any fixed class of machines and let b(M,c,d,m) denote [S_M(m) > s(m)^c or tau_M(m) > s(m)^d]. If (40a) is read as forall M in C, forall c,d, forall m0, exists m >= m0: b(M,c,d,m), then there is no M in C and no fixed c,d for which both bounds hold for every sufficiently large m. Proof: suppose such M,c,d exist, with threshold m1. Apply (40a) to that M,c,d and m0=m1. Its witness m >= m1 has b(M,c,d,m) true, contradicting the assumed two bounds at every m >= m1. Conversely, if no such eventual-fast triple exists, then for each M,c,d and each m0 there must be some m >= m0 where at least one bound fails; otherwise both bounds hold for all m >= m0. Thus the two formulations are equivalent for the same quantified class C. This repairs only the quantifier step: it does not transfer from C to a different MMW machine class.

label: S0008
statement:
statement: For any functions S, tau on the stream-exponent indices m in N, and any fixed bounds b1(m), b2(m), the statement forall m0 exists m>=m0 [S(m)>b1(m) or tau(m)>b2(m)] is equivalent to the nonexistence of a tail [m1,infinity) on which both bounds hold pointwise. For the manuscript encoding N=2^m stream bits, this uses the same exponent m as MMW's parameter whenever MMW indexes a length-N truth table as N=2^n; the map is n=m, not n=2^m.
derivation: Let Bad(m) be S(m)>b1(m) or tau(m)>b2(m). If forall m0 exists m>=m0 Bad(m), then no m1 can satisfy forall m>=m1 not Bad(m), since taking m0=m1 would produce a contradiction. Conversely, if there is no such m1, then for each m0 the suffix m>=m0 contains some Bad(m), which is precisely the displayed statement. Under the manuscript's explicit stream length 2^m, MMW's truth-table exponent n denotes the integer satisfying stream length 2^n; equality 2^m=2^n gives m=n. The independent finite truth-table check verified the logical identity for all paired Boolean cost tables at horizons 1 through 6; the proof itself is the argument above.

statement:
statement: Conditional resource-transfer lemma. Let s:N→N satisfy s(m)≥m. Let C be the machine class quantified by (40a), with resources S_M(m), τ_M(m), and D a target streaming class. Assume every T∈D has a simulator M_T∈C and constants a,b,r≥1 such that for every m, S_{M_T}(m)≤a(s(m)+S_T(m))^r and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b(s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m))^r, with identical input lengths, exact output relation, and oracle convention. If T has S_T(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_T(m)≤s(m)^d for all m≥m₀, then M_T has S_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₁ and τ_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₂ for all sufficiently large m, for fixed exponents C₁,C₂. Consequently (40a) rules out every such eventually polynomially bounded T∈D.
derivation: Let k=max(c,d,1). For m≥max(m₀,2), s(m)≥m≥2, hence s(m)+S_T(m)≤2s(m)^k and s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m)≤3s(m)^k. Thus S_{M_T}(m)≤a2^r s(m)^(kr) and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b3^r s(m)^(kr). Choose fixed integers C₁,C₂ large enough to absorb the constants into extra powers of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Then both simulator resources are bounded by s(m)^C₁ and s(m)^C₂ throughout a tail. This contradicts (40a) instantiated with M_T,C₁,C₂ and that tail threshold, which requires some length in the tail violating at least one bound. Therefore no such T exists. This is conditional on the stated same-index exact simulation and matching oracle/resource hypotheses.

label: S0013
statement:
statement_start: Conditional index-transfer lemma: Let source lengths m range over the positive integers, let target lengths be f(m) with f(m) tending to infinity, and suppose a target streaming algorithm T has eventual polynomial resource bounds.
derivation: Let s(m) be the source parameter with s(m)>=m. Suppose T at target length f(m) uses space at most s(f(m))^c and update time at most s(f(m))^d for all sufficiently large target lengths. Suppose an exact source simulator M on length m has S_M(m)<=a(s(m)+S_T(f(m)))^r and tau_M(m)<=b(s(m)+S_T(f(m))+tau_T(f(m)))^r for fixed a,b,r, and suppose s(f(m))<=s(m)^q for all sufficiently large m. Since f(m)->infinity, there is m0 such that f(m) is beyond T's resource-bound threshold for every m>=m0. For such m, s(f(m))^c<=s(m)^(qc), and similarly for d. Set k=max(1,qc,qd). Then both simulator resource bounds are at most a(2s(m)^k)^r and b(3s(m)^k)^r. Since s(m)>=m tends to infinity, fixed multiplicative constants are absorbed by increasing the exponents, so S_M and tau_M are each bounded by a fixed power of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Exact simulation preserves the problem's answer. The lemma is conditional on the stated parameter comparison and exact simulation; it does not prove either exists for the MMW/manuscript models.

label: S0015
statement:
statement_start: Fixed-pair quantifier equivalence: Fix an admissible pair (s,A) and a fixed class C of exact machines with resource functions S_M(m), tau_M(m). The assertion that for every M in C and c,d in N there exists m0 such that for every m>=m0 at least one bound fails is equivalent to the assertion that there do not exist M in C and c,d in N such that both resource bounds hold on a tail.
derivation: For each fixed tuple (M,c,d), let B(m) mean S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. The assertion is forall (M,c,d), forall m0, exists m>=m0, not B(m). Its negation is exists (M,c,d), exists m0, forall m>=m0, B(m), by quantifier negation and De Morgan's law. Thus it is exactly the absence of an eventually jointly bounded machine in C. statement: Conditional per-read oracle-elimination composition lemma. Let s(m)≥m. Suppose a deterministic one-pass streaming machine uses at most s(m)^a elementary steps and makes at most s(m)^a oracle queries in each interval between successive input reads, including final reporting. Suppose each query has length at most s(m)^b, and each queried language has a fixed uniform deterministic decider using time and space at most L^k on length-L inputs, for fixed k. Replacing each oracle query by that decider gives an oracle-free uniform one-pass machine with per-read time O(s(m)^(a+bk)) and space O(s(m)^max(a,bk)), up to fixed polynomial simulation overhead, while preserving the stream and output relation. Proof: simulate each transition, saving each query string, running its decider, and returning its answer. At most s^a queries of cost at most s^(bk) occur per interval, in addition to at most s^a original steps. Query workspace is O(s^(bk)); original state and query-generation workspace is O(s^a). This also applies to final reporting. Since every returned answer equals the oracle language’s truth value, induction over transitions gives identical states after each read and the same output. The lemma is conditional on the stated query-count, query-length, and uniform-decider bounds; it does not establish that MMW’s exact algorithm meets them or that (40a) holds.

label: S0046
statement:
statement: Repaired conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Let s(m)>=m be time-constructible. Fix a uniform one-pass oracle machine U and fixed constants a,b,c,e,q. For every m and every stream input of length 2^m, assume U uses at most s(m)^a space, makes at most s(m)^b oracle queries between consecutive reads, each of length at most s(m)^c, and performs at most s(m)^q non-oracle steps between those reads; impose the same bounds on final reporting. If the oracle language has a fixed deterministic decider using O(l^e) time and space on queries of length l, then replacing each oracle call by that decider yields a uniform oracle-free one-pass simulation with polynomial-in-s(m) space and worst-case time per inter-read interval and final report. Proof: execute U's non-oracle transitions unchanged. For each oracle query of length l<=s(m)^c, run the fixed decider, costing O(s(m)^(ce)) time and space. At most s(m)^b calls per interval cost O(s(m)^(b+ce)) total time. The simulator's space is bounded by the original configuration space plus one query of length at most s(m)^c plus the decider workspace O(s(m)^(ce)); this is polynomial in s(m). Non-oracle work contributes at most s(m)^q. Thus both time and space are bounded by s(m)^d times a constant for some fixed d depending only on a,b,c,e,q. Uniformity holds because U and the decider are fixed algorithms. The claim is conditional: it does not establish these hypotheses for the exact MMW procedure or the class match required by (40a).
scope: Conditional simulation theorem for uniform one-pass oracle machines with explicit per-interval non-oracle-time, query-count, query-length, and workspace bounds; no claim about the exact MMW setup or P!=NP.
proof: As stated in the step.
